title: Review: A simple model of the atom, symbols, relative atomic mass, electronic charge and isotopes
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank for AQA GCSE Chemistry (8462) (review status in the bank: authored-gated-unreviewed). Clues: 4.1.1-c29 first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.1.1-c03 first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.1.1-c14 first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.1.1-c05 first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: 4.1.1-q29, 4.1.1-q38, 4.1.1-q40, 4.1.1-q46, 4.1.1-q27, 4.1.1-q36, 4.1.1-q39, 4.1.1-q43, 4.1.1-q26, 4.1.1-q30, 4.1.1-q41, 4.1.1-q28. assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Nucleus
items.clue: The centre of the atom, containing almost all of its mass, with a radius less than 1/10 000 of that of the atom (about 1 x 10⁻¹⁴ m).

items.label: Chemical symbol
items.clue: The one- or two-letter code used to represent an atom of an element, eg O represents an atom of oxygen and Na represents an atom of sodium.

items.label: Simple distillation
items.clue: A physical process that separates a solvent from a solution by boiling it off and condensing the vapour, leaving the dissolved solid behind.

items.label: Compound
items.clue: A substance containing two or more elements chemically combined in fixed proportions, represented by a formula built from the symbols of the atoms it was formed from.

questions.stem: Two atoms each have 6 protons but different masses. What must be true?

options.text: They are atoms of different elements
They must have different numbers of electrons
They are atoms of the same element
They must have different numbers of protons

questions.explanation: All atoms of a particular element have the same number of protons.

questions.stem: A chloride ion is written Cl⁻. A chlorine atom has atomic number 17. Which is correct for the ion?

options.text: 16 protons and 17 electrons, one proton lost
18 protons and 18 electrons, since it is neutral
17 protons and 17 electrons, as they stay equal
17 protons and 18 electrons, as one is gained

questions.explanation: The 1− charge shows one extra electron; the number of protons is unchanged.

questions.stem: Lithium has two isotopes: 7.5% is ⁶Li and 92.5% is ⁷Li. What is the relative atomic mass of lithium?
A shell diagram is drawn with 4 electrons on the outer ring, 8 on the middle ring and 2 on the inner ring. Which electronic structure does it show?
questions.explanation: The structure starts at the innermost ring: 2, then 8, then 4.

questions.stem: An atom has 11 protons. How many electrons does it have, and why?

options.text: 0, because neutrons make the atom neutral overall
23, because protons and neutrons are added together
10, because it loses one of its protons
11, because electrons and protons are equal in number

questions.explanation: In an atom the number of electrons equals the number of protons.

options.text: Atoms of the same element but with different numbers of protons
Atoms of the same element with different numbers of electrons
Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons
Atoms of different elements with the same mass number

questions.explanation: This is the specification's definition of isotopes.

questions.stem: What does the relative atomic mass of an element take account of?

options.text: The abundance of each of its isotopes
The mass number of its commonest isotope
The average of its isotope mass numbers
The number of protons and neutrons combined

questions.explanation: Relative atomic mass is an average that takes account of isotope abundance.

questions.stem: The electronic structure of sodium is 2,8,1. What does the final 1 tell you?

options.text: There is one electron in the third energy level
There is one electron in the innermost shell only
One of the shells in the atom is completely full
The last shell was filled up first of all

questions.explanation: The numbers are read outwards, so the last one is the outermost level.

questions.stem: What are the relative electrical charges of a proton, a neutron and an electron?

options.text: Proton and neutron +1, electron −1
Proton +1, neutron 0, electron −1
Proton 0, neutron +1 and electron −1
Every particle has a charge of +1 or −1

questions.explanation: These are the relative electrical charges given in the specification.

questions.stem: What is the approximate radius of an atom?

options.text: 0.1 nm (1 x 10⁻¹⁰ m)

questions.explanation: This is the value given in the specification.

questions.stem: In which order do electrons occupy the energy levels (shells) of an atom?

options.text: The outer shell is filled before the inner ones
They spread out evenly between the shells
The lowest available energy level is filled first
The first shell takes eight electrons first

questions.explanation: Electrons occupy the lowest available energy levels, the innermost available shells.

questions.stem: What does the atomic number of an element tell you?

options.text: The total of the protons and neutrons
The number of protons in each atom
The number of neutrons inside each atom
The number of electrons per shell

questions.explanation: The number of protons in an atom of an element is its atomic number.
